question.text: Mr. Ashwin Mehra, the GP of 'Yamuna Growth Fund III', is negotiating with an anchor LP (an insurance company) committing INR 250 crore out of a target INR 1,000 crore. The LP demands a 'management fee step-down' post the commitment period. From a manager's negotiation perspective, which of the following is the MOST appropriate structure?

answer.text: Refuse any step-down — management fee must be flat for the full fund life to cover operating costs
Step down fees to zero immediately after first close to attract more capital

Agree to a step-down where the management fee is charged on committed capital during the commitment period and is later reduced to invested capital or AUM after the commitment period, in line with the fee structures permitted in the workbook
Shift the fee to a pure performance-only model with no base fee at all

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, for Category I/II AIFs management fees are typically charged on committed capital during the commitment period and may later be reduced to invested capital or AUM. The workbook also notes that LP negotiations frequently drive down management-fee and expense structures, so a structured step-down post the commitment period is a permitted and commonly negotiated arrangement. The Trap: A purely flat lifetime fee on commitments ignores the workbook's allowance for a reduced basis post the commitment period. An immediate step-down to zero would not cover ongoing operating costs and is not what the workbook contemplates. A pure performance-only model with no base fee is not the typical Category I/II structure described. Note: The defining feature of the step-down is the change in base — committed capital during the commitment period, then invested capital or AUM after — rather than any specific headline percentage.
